rationale: The native GGML header stores signed int32 fields. Decoding the little-endian bits as int32 is intentional; negative fields and invalid dimensions are rejected immediately before use.
The RIFF size comparison cannot accept truncation: the same boolean expression requires size-8 <= MaxUint32. The caller rejects sizes below 46 and bounds the upload before validation.
pcmOutput caps every write at maxData, which is at most MaxUint32-36. Its locked written counter is positive and even before conversion to the RIFF uint32 size.

The executable and optional prefix arguments are operator configuration. Request audio is supplied through bounded stdin; decoder arguments are fixed and no shell or uploaded filename is executed. Cancellation kills and reaps the process group.

Both subprocess executables are operator-selected commands copied into typed supervisor options. Native/GPU arguments use fixed flags and validated startup values; no shell or client argument is used. The supervisor owns bounded process-group retirement.

The goroutine owns process shutdown after the serving context has ended. A fresh background-derived context intentionally permits graceful drain; both HTTP shutdown and its wait are bounded by the configured drain/cleanup budgets.

The unrooted branch opens only an operator-configured prepared-model path, never a client-supplied filename. Downloaded cache paths use os.Root with O_NOFOLLOW. Both branches verify the opened descriptor is a regular file; provisioning verifies its configured SHA256.

The advisory concerns Echo Proxy WebSocket middleware. Resident V1 uses explicit HTTP handlers and its own bounded http.Client transport; Echo Proxy is not referenced or linked into either entrypoint. The mandatory compiled-symbol scope test checks both exact Linux/amd64 entrypoints and includes a positive Proxy-linked fixture. Echo v5.4.0 remains the approved core pin; this is exact non-applicability, not an accepted-risk waiver.
